title: Knowledge check: Frontend Integration Patterns

questions.prompt: Which topic is explicitly listed for “Frontend Integration Patterns”?
options: A complete substitute for server-side validation
A guarantee that every database write succeeds atomically
A feature that is always enabled without configuration
questions.explanation: The supplied Django curriculum lists “Django templates with static assets” under lesson 253, “Frontend Integration Patterns”. The lesson connects this item to the practical Django workflow for localization, accessibility, and user experience.

questions.prompt: Which workflow best supports reliable work on “Frontend Integration Patterns”?
options: Assume the browser is trusted and skip server-side checks.
Copy a production secret into the source file so every environment matches.
Publish an example before checking framework/version compatibility.
Use a documented small example, verify expected behavior, and test an invalid or boundary case.
questions.answer_key: Use a documented small example, verify expected behavior, and test an invalid or boundary case.
questions.explanation: Small reproducible examples, server-side validation where relevant, and explicit positive/negative checks help distinguish expected behavior from assumptions. Version, environment, and boundary cases should be documented.

questions.prompt: Which practice is most appropriate when applying “Frontend Integration Patterns” in a real application?
options: Assume framework defaults replace application authorization rules.
Change multiple variables at once, then guess what fixed the issue.
Keep behavior explicit, validate at the correct boundary, and verify both success and failure paths.
Rely on a visual inspection alone.
questions.answer_key: Keep behavior explicit, validate at the correct boundary, and verify both success and failure paths.
questions.explanation: The lesson is part of Localization, Accessibility, and User Experience. Select the approach that supports correctness, safe handling of failures, and verifiable behavior; see the linked official documentation for version-specific details.

notes: Answer keys and explanations remain in the server-side course repository. The existing CodeLeaf GET handler strips answers until grading; this course does not expose solutions in public lesson content.
